layers.note: A mounded shrub of rocky slopes and the banks of washes.

moisture.note: Dry rocky slopes and sandy washes.

elevation_m.note: About 400 to 1,070 m in Arizona (Kearney and Peebles: 1,300 to 3,500 feet), near sea level in the Colorado Desert.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about 8 to 22 °C; gone below 5 °C and above 25 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −7 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −10 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 28 to 37 °C; gone below 26 °C, where summers are too short, and above 40 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 6,000 to 12,500 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 5,000.

degree_days_5.note: About 4,200 to 10,500 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 3,500.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.03, gone by 0.01.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: it grows where winter rain falls alone (the Mojave and the low Colorado Desert) as well as where the July to September monsoon brings summer rain, as on the bajada (about half the year's); up to about 0.8 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.9.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m) from general knowledge of the species, the ranges and elevations in Kearney and Peebles (1942) and, where one exists, the FEIS species review. Chuparosa grows in southern Arizona, southeastern California and northwestern Mexico (Kearney and Peebles 1942), in the frost-light Sonoran and Colorado deserts. Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
